sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: revocation, suspension, violation points, impound and court enforcement
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from this section's selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge or memory.
The revocation offense list is introduced at the foot of the previous page as not limited to the items shown; the items on the first selected page are taught as examples, not a complete list [A01].
The vehicle impound list on the first selected page joins its last two conditions with a stray and, so it is unclear whether lacking financial responsibility and being in a crash are separate grounds or one combined ground; neither is taught (verify AZ-POINTS-D-IMPOUND) [A01].
The ground about being convicted as a driver in a crash begins at the foot of the second selected page and finishes on the last; it is taught from the last page, where it is complete [A03].
The nitrous oxide paragraph on the last selected page continues on the next page; only the prohibited act is taught here, not its penalty [A03].
Originality: every statement is reworded from the cited page; no manual sentence, table, image or official test question is reproduced.
Exam numbers: the manual prints no question count, passing score, item format or time limit, so none is stated anywhere in this section; the typed debts live in part A.
External review: restating published Arizona traffic and licensing rules needs no clinical or legal sign-off; none is requested.

corpus_stability.reason: The Arizona Driver License Manual carries one revision line on its contents page (Revised September 2026) and points to Arizona Revised Statutes Title 28 for current law; nothing in the selected pages signals more than one rewrite per year.

verification_debt.claim_text: The manual's vehicle impound list ends with a financial responsibility item followed by a stray and, then a crash item; confirm with an official MVD or statute source whether these are separate impound grounds or one combined ground before teaching either.
